description: Team of first-semester Aerospace Engineering students at ENES Juriquilla, UNAM.
summary: Design, build, and lead your own space mission in this interactive 3D simulator. The game guides you in an educational, hands-on way through every stage of aerospace planning: define your objectives, configure your rocket's components, and take control during orbital flight or descent. With total freedom to adjust parameters and optimize resources, you'll discover that there is no single right answer and that every decision requires prioritizing different technical requirements. Beyond the design phase, you'll have to prove your precision across three challenging minigames to reach the ideal orbit, achieve a flawless landing, and clear away the lunar dust
details:
Zafemun Mission is a simulation video game in which you take on the role of an engineer tasked with designing a space mission. At the start, you choose the mission's difficulty level, which determines the objective—ranging from placing a satellite into orbit, deploying a rover on the Moon or executing a crewed lunar landing. You will select the essential tools required to measure and complete secondary objectives, design your rocket, define the target orbit, and—if necessary—choose the appropriate spacesuits for your crew, among other critical decisions. As you make these choices, you must account for various factors such as mass, budget, and energy generation and consumption; these variables will ultimately determine the success—and the probability of success—of your mission. It is important to note that there is no single, predetermined path to success or failure; the game offers complete freedom to explore different parameters and experiment with various available components, all while striving to optimize your mission. Don’t worry if you aren’t familiar with every aspect of space exploration—the game provides detailed descriptions for every tool and system to guide you. Beyond configuring mission parameters, the game challenges your skills through a series of minigames, requiring you to identify the optimal orbit, ensure a safe descent, and execute a perfect landing. Zafemun Mission bridges the gap between theoretical space mission concepts and practical application, ensuring that you remain fully aware of the impact—whether in terms of savings or waste—of every technical decision you make. At the end of each mission, you will receive a mission report detailing your success rate, areas for improvement, items that were misused or “wasted,” observations, and the most optimal way the mission could have been completed. Consequently, the more missions you undertake and the more variables you adjust while playing, the more you will learn from each experience.

 Impact

Through this project, we hope that young people can delve into the science of designing and executing a space mission, regardless of their prior knowledge on the subject. Our goal is for the new generation to gain a broader perspective on the complexity and the challenges that must be addressed when carrying out a space mission—an experience that will foster diverse ways of thinking, leading to the development of new and innovative solutions to complex problems.

Tools, coding lenguaje, and software

For the development of the video game, we use two tools that work in tandem: VS Code, an advanced code editor that serves as our primary development environment for writing, organizing, and debugging all project scripts and programming logic; and Godot Engine, the game engine we employ to design the 3D environment, manage physics, render interactive scenes, and visually assemble all the mechanics and the interface for the space missions. The programming language used for the project is GDScript—a language native to Godot designed for controlling nodes, game physics, and 3D scenes—which is, however, very similar to Python.
